summary: The study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of silicon dioxide using aminosilanes DSBAS and BTBAS with ozone as the coreactant. The process involves the reaction of the aminosilanes with surface OH groups, forming Si−O−SiH3 and Si−O−SiH2−(NHtBu) species. The transformation of these species into bidentate and tridentate bonding depends on the initial OH concentration and ozone flux. The study highlights the importance of ozone flux in achieving complete ligand exchange and the formation of stoichiometric silicon oxide.
evidence: The text states that the study uses in situ Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy to investigate silicon dioxide deposition on OH-terminated oxidized Si(100) surfaces using DSBAS and BTBAS with ozone as the coreactant. It also mentions that the process type is thermal ALD and that the temperature range is 100 °C.
